 Judgment

Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 11.06.2019 passed by the Principal Senior Civil Judge,
Member MACT-IV, Davanagere (for short 'the Tribunal'), in MVC No.672/2018, the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
That on 08.04.2018, the petitioner along with his wife were moving in the motor bike bearing registration No.KA- 26/R-8096 and at about 6.00 p.m. when they reached near Hanagavadi Harihar Taluk in front of Veereshwara Rice Mill, an auto bearing registration No.KA-17/C-8898 being driven in a rash and negligent manner and duly insured with the second respondent came and dashed the motor bike, because of which, the petitioner sustained the following injuries:-
1) Swelling of the lower part of thigh left side.
2) Injury to lower part of anterior part of the thigh.
3) Knee left hematoma present 4) Femur on lower end left side exposed (comminuted)
4.
Therefore, the petitioner has preferred MVC No.672/2018.

The Tribunal, based on the evidence Rajashekar Kammar vs Dadabuden R on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156549421/

Food & nourishment, attendant 2 Rs. 20,000/-
& conveyance charges Loss of income during laid up 3 Rs. 27,000/-
period 4 Medical expenses Rs.1,69,200/-
5 Loss of earning due to disability Rs.1,68,480/- Loss of amenities and 6 Rs. 10,000/-
 unhappiness
Not satisfied by the same, the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.
6. The accident happened in the year 2018.
The petitioner was aged 49 years.
His income has not been established before the Tribunal.
Hence, the notional income as prescribed in the Lok-Adalath chart has to be considered which will be Rs.12,500/- per month.

The petitioner has suffered 38%
permanent disability to the left leg.
The Tribunal has assessed the total body disability at 12% and awarded a sum of Rs.1,68,480/- towards 'loss of earning due to disability'.
In my opinion, based on the Doctor's evidence, it ought to have taken the total body disability at 12.66%.
The petitioner was aged 49 years at the time of accident.
Hence, the multiplier of '13' has to be adopted as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma & Ors vs Delhi Transport Corp.& Anr reported in 2009(6) SCC 121.

sentences.text: Thus, towards 'loss of earning due to disability', the petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.2,46,870/-(12500x12x13x12.66%).
The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.27,000/- towards 'loss of income during laid up period'.

Given the nature of injuries, the laid up period has to be considered atleast 5 months and a sum of Rs.62,500/- (12,500x5=62,500/-)
is awarded under this head.
Towards 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/-.
Given the nature of injuries, I am of the opinion that a sum of Rs.50,000/- would be just and fair in this regard.
Towards 'food, nourishment, attendant & conveyance charges, a sum of Rs.20,000/- has been awarded by the Tribunal.
In my opinion, the same is appropriate.
The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,69,200/- towards 'medical expenses' based on the actual bills submitted by the petitioner.
In my opinion, the same is just and reasonable.
Towards 'loss of amenities and unhappiness' the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/-.
In my opinion, it would be appropriate to enhance it to Rs.25,000/-.
Further , the Doctor has opined that petitioner requires surgery for removal of implants in his knee and it would cost around Rs.35,000/- to Rs.40,000/-.
